title: Students and youth in Croatia strike over living costs and war

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against high living costs, housing affordability, and issues in the education and healthcare sectors.
tea.want: The movement demands affordable housing, transparent employment processes, demilitarization, and improved environmental protections.
tea.changed: Nov 20: Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs criticized the strike as politicized and threatened students with unexcused absences.

summary: On November 20, 2026, students and high schoolers across Croatia participated in a nationwide strike organized by the initiative Štrajk mladih. The action, part of the international International Youth Strike movement, took place in cities including Zagreb, Rijeka, Pula, Zadar, and Osijek. Participants are protesting against rising living costs, the lack of affordable housing, and systemic issues in education and healthcare. The movement also advocates for demilitarization and environmental protection under the slogan "For our future, not their wars." Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs dismissed the organizers as anarchists, accusing them of political manipulation and warning that students who skip classes will receive unexcused absences. Organizers stated that the strike is a grassroots effort and that they intend to continue their activities beyond this one-day boycott.
response: Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs labeled the protesters as anarchists involved in political activities and announced that students who participate in the strike will be marked with unexcused absences.

updates.text: Students and youth across Croatia participate in a strike organized by Štrajk mladih to protest living costs and war.
Minister of Education Radovan Fuchs criticizes the strike and threatens participants with unexcused absences.
